fields.name: name
fields.description: Unique node identifier used for identity and lookup. Requirements: lowercase_snake_case, immutable once created, globally unique within the graph.

fields.name: label
fields.description: Human-readable display name shown in the UI. Can include spaces and capitalization; not used for identity.

fields.name: type
fields.description: Node taxonomy; must match one of nodeTypes[].name.

fields.name: description
fields.description: Optional free-text context or rationale not modeled as separate nodes; prefer structured graph facts when possible.

fields.name: scope
fields.description: Business units the node belongs to, comma-separated (for example uc or uc,nc). Set it for business-unit specific concepts and when the input states which units use the node; otherwise leave it empty. Use common only when the input says every unit shares the node; never combine common with other values.

fields.name: sourceName
fields.description: Source node name. Must reference an existing node; immutable for relation identity.

fields.name: targetName
fields.description: Target node name. Must reference an existing node; immutable for relation identity.

fields.name: relation
fields.description: Relation type; must match one of relationshipTypes[].name. Part of relation identity; use lowercase_snake_case.

fields.name: information
fields.description: Single-line contextual note about the relationship (e.g., 'on click of Next button'). Use for UX/state/transport details clarifying the link.

fields.name: description
fields.description: Optional longer rationale or operational notes about the relation; use sparingly.

fields.name: scope
fields.description: Business units the relation applies to, comma-separated. Leave it empty in almost all cases; set it only when the input says the relation applies to specific units while its endpoints are shared.

fields.name: metadata
fields.description: Optional machine-readable flags used by the ingestion engine (e.g., 'AMBIGUITY:<reason>', 'CONTRADICTION:<reason>').
